name: Almost All
description: You are given a tree with $$$n$$$ nodes. You have to write non-negative integers on its edges so that the following condition would be satisfied: For every two nodes $$$i$$$, $$$j$$$, look at the path between them and count the sum of numbers on the edges of this path. Write all obtained sums on the blackboard. Then every integer from $$$1$$$ to $$$\lfloor \frac{2n^2}{9} \rfloor$$$ has to be written on the blackboard at least once. It is guaranteed that such an arrangement exists.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 1000$$$) — the number of nodes. Each of the next $$$n-1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$, $$$u \neq v$$$), meaning that there is an edge between nodes $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. It is guaranteed that these edges form a tree.
output_specification: Output $$$n-1$$$ lines, each of form $$$u$$$ $$$v$$$ $$$x$$$ ($$$0 \le x \le 10^6$$$), which will mean that you wrote number $$$x$$$ on the edge between $$$u$$$, $$$v$$$. Set of edges $$$(u, v)$$$ has to coincide with the set of edges of the input graph, but you can output edges in any order. You can also output ends of edges in an order different from the order in input.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1205D — Almost All [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
